domain_setting: A clear natural-history field guide showing landforms, habitats, and waterways in a shared calm landscape palette, with close framing where one defining feature should dominate.
global_art_direction: Make the specific landform or habitat the first-read silhouette; use a simple horizon and a few scale cues instead of a busy postcard.

Distinguish similar siblings by their profile and view: hill is low and rounded, mountain is one tall mass, mountain range has repeated peaks, peak is one sharp summit, plain is broad level land, plateau is elevated with a flat top, and valley is a low corridor between high sides.
For water terms, show relative shape and motion: small still pond, larger enclosed lake, narrow stream, winding river, turbulent rapids, and a vertical waterfall.
Differentiate glacier as a broad grounded ice tongue, iceberg as a floating broken mass, polar region as an expansive frozen environment, and sea/ocean/coast by framing and shoreline relationship.
Avoid readable words, letters, numbers, maps with labels, logos, or signs. Use unmarked shapes and natural context.

reviewed_existing_art.reason: The six available legacy pictures were reviewed. The Mulberry hedge, pond, and beach pictograms use a mismatched neon/clip-art style; the OpenMoji mountain, volcano, and desert silhouettes are too generic and under-detailed for the target terms and the course style.

entries.canyon: A deep, narrow gorge with steep rock walls, shown in cross-section perspective with a small winding river far below.
entries.cave: A dark natural opening in a rocky hillside, with a clearly visible arched entrance and receding interior.
entries.cliff: A steep near-vertical rock face dropping directly to the sea, with a narrow ledge and surf far below.
entries.hill: One modest rounded rise with a gentle slope and low height, distinct from a tall mountain.
entries.mountain: One prominent high, steep mountain mass with a defined summit and rocky foothills.
entries.mountain range: A continuous chain of several overlapping high peaks extending across the horizon.
entries.peak: One pointed summit emphasized above the surrounding lower ridge.
entries.plain (landscape): A broad, level expanse of open land with a distant low horizon; use the geographical noun sense, not the adjective meaning clear or ordinary.
entries.plateau: A broad elevated landform with steep sides and a wide, flat top.
entries.rocks: A small group of separate, irregular boulders of varied size, shown as solid stones on bare ground.
entries.sand dune: A smooth crescent-shaped hill of wind-sculpted sand with a windward slope and a sharper lee crest.
entries.valley: A low corridor between two elevated slopes, with a stream leading toward the distant opening.
entries.volcano: A single conical volcanic mountain with an open summit crater and a restrained plume of ash and steam.
entries.countryside: A broad rural view with patchwork fields, a winding lane, scattered homes, and distant tree lines.
entries.desert: A wide arid region with sparse vegetation, bare rock, and heat-softened distant ridges; do not reduce it to one dune.
entries.farmland: Managed crop land with long parallel furrows and an orderly boundary beside a farm track.
entries.field (land): One open grassy tract bounded by a low fence, without crop rows or flowers as the main cue.
entries.forest: A dense, continuous stand of mature trees with overlapping trunks and canopy.
entries.geographical features: An educational landscape overview combining distinct mountains, a river, a plain, and coastline as a broad composite scene.
entries.grassland: An open expanse dominated by tall grasses and low rolling ground, with very few trees.
entries.hedge: A trimmed continuous row of dense shrubs forming a clear garden boundary.
entries.landscape: A composed scenic view of a natural valley, distant mountains, water, and foreground, emphasizing the whole view.
entries.meadow: A lush grassy clearing dotted with small wildflowers and framed by a few trees.
entries.oasis: A small green pool and palm grove surrounded by dry desert on every side.
entries.polar region: A vast cold environment with snowfields, ice, distant glaciers, and very sparse life.
entries.rain forest / rainforest: A dense warm tropical forest with layered broadleaf canopy, vines, and lush undergrowth.
entries.swamp: A low wetland with still shallow water, emergent reeds, and tangled trees rooted in saturated ground.
entries.geyser: A natural hot spring erupting a tall column of water and steam from a rocky vent.
entries.lake: A broad inland body of still water enclosed by land, with an unbroken shore and reflections.
entries.pond: A small still freshwater pool close to the viewer, edged by grass and reeds.
entries.rapids: A river section where fast water surges through rocks, broken into white foam and turbulence.
entries.river: A wide flowing body of water meandering through a large landscape toward the horizon.
entries.stream: A narrow shallow flow of clear water winding through grass and small stones.
entries.waterfall: A large vertical sheet of river water dropping over a rock ledge into a basin.
entries.beach: A sandy shore with a broad foreground beach meeting gentle ocean surf.
entries.coast: The edge where land and sea meet, shown as a long rocky shoreline curving into the distance.
entries.glacier: A massive slow-moving body of grounded blue-white ice flowing down a mountain valley.
entries.high tide: A shoreline at its highest water level, with waves reaching the upper edge of a coastal marker or seawall.
entries.iceberg: A large floating piece of broken glacial ice with a broad visible tip and a submerged blue mass beneath the waterline.
entries.island: A distinct piece of land completely surrounded by water, shown with shoreline visible all around it.
entries.low tide: A shoreline with water drawn far back, exposing a wide band of wet sand and shallow tide pools.
entries.ocean: An immense open expanse of deep water with a far horizon and no nearby land enclosing it.
entries.sea: A broad coastal body of water framed by two nearby headlands to show its relation to land.
